personality_one_liner: A highly readable, stable, and professional enterprise interface that prioritizes clear data presentation, trustworthy corporate aesthetics, and efficient task execution.

spacing.rule: Use native iOS comfortable vertical rhythms. Provide generous padding around enterprise content to avoid overly dense, cramped dashboards. Adhere strictly to these tokens.

do's: Sticky headers over scrolling lists (Customer list, Task list)
Bottom tab bar when content scrolls behind it
Featured summary card overlay on the dashboard hero image
dont's: Standard list rows in the employee directory

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Provide a high-level summary of active tasks, urgent tenders, and attendance metrics.

states.loading: Centered spinner over the main canvas.
states.empty: Illustration of a clean desk with a message indicating no immediate actions required today.
states.error: Readable error message 'Unable to load dashboard' with a primary Retry CTA.

screens.layout: Top section features a hero image of a professional office (using dashboard_hero URL) with a vertical gradient scrim (transparent to ≥70% surfaceInverse). A glass-effect summary card sits over the scrim displaying high-level metrics. Below this, a 2-column grid displays quick stats (Accounts, HR), followed by a list of 3 urgent tenders tagged with the red 'error' color token for urgency.

screens.name: Business
screens.purpose: Central hub for managing the Customer Database and Accounts.

states.loading: Skeleton list rows matching the customer/invoice card shapes.
states.empty: Abstract document illustration with text 'No business records yet' and a CTA to 'Add Customer'.
states.error: Error reading database, with a retry button.

screens.layout: A sticky segmented control at the top to toggle between 'Customers' and 'Accounts'. Customer list uses initial-avatars (fallback) or real company logos, with full-width cards. Accounts list emphasizes financial values using the green 'success' color for paid and red 'error' color for pending. A sticky FAB (glass or brandPrimary solid) at the bottom right for adding new records.

screens.name: Tasks
screens.purpose: Manage assigned tasks, deadlines, and employee workloads.

states.empty: Uses the 'empty_tasks' abstract 3D folder image. 'All caught up!' message with a CTA to assign a task.
states.error: Network error with a retry button.

screens.layout: Top tab filters for To-Do, Doing, Done. Task cards have a minimum 56pt height, incorporating checkboxes, assignee avatars, and priority badges. Use status-based grouping per Mobbin enterprise standards to improve glanceability. Sticky primary CTA to 'Create Task' at the bottom.

screens.name: More
screens.purpose: Access point for the Tender Library, HR/Employee Directory, and App Settings.

states.error: Failed to load directory/tenders, with retry.

screens.layout: Standard iOS native settings list structure. Grouped rows for 'Tender Library', 'HR & Directory', and 'Profile'. Every row features a leading icon inside a brandTertiary-tinted rounded square container, the title, and a trailing chevron. Navigation pushes to detail screens for specific modules.

empty_tasks.alt: Abstract blue 3D document folder indicating no active items

instructions_to_main_agent: The user explicitly requested a 'Blue, Red, Green' scheme. Blue is permitted as the brand primary (Trust). Red must be used strictly for alerts/urgent tenders (error token). Green must be used for success/paid statuses (success token). Do not use these colors decoratively.

Implement the '1 iOS-Native Clean' personality. Avoid overly dense 'web dashboard' style layouts; ensure generous md/lg padding and single-column full-width cards or proper 2-column grids with space-between.
The Dashboard hero image MUST be overlaid with a top-to-bottom linear gradient scrim (transparent to >=70% surfaceInverse) to guarantee foreground text readability.
All interactive elements must respect a minimum touch target size of 44x44pt.
For the bottom navigation, use a maximum of 4 tabs: Dashboard, Business, Tasks, and More.
When displaying lists of customers or employees, always attempt to fetch real logos or avatars first. Use initial-based avatars strictly as a fallback.
Remember to include proper Loading, Empty, and Error states mapping exactly to the full screen flex view.
For sticky CTA buttons, wrap them in a fixed container outside the scrolling ScrollView and pad the bottom of the ScrollView appropriately.
